title: Singleton mass times log-likelihood ratio
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite discrete measurable space, let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$. Writing $\mu(\{\omega\})$ and $
u(\{\omega\})$ for the (real-valued) masses of the singleton $\{\omega\}$ and $\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the log-likelihood ratio of $\mu$ against $
u$, one has
\[
  \mu(\{\omega\}) \cdot \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(\omega)
  = \mu(\{\omega\}) \cdot \log\!\left( rac{\mu(\{\omega\})}{
u(\{\omega\})}ight).
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ absolutely continuous with respect to ν
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space, $\mu \ll \nu$ finite measures, and $\omega \in \Omega$.
Then
\[
  \mu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\} \cdot \mathrm{llr}(\mu,\nu,\omega)
  = \mu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\}
    \cdot \log\!\left(
      \frac{\mu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\}}{\nu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\}}
    \right).
\]
